name: Ascot / cravat

lead: An ascot or cravat is a piece of cloth worn around the neck, typically tucked inside an open shirt collar. It draws attention to the neck and face and gives an outfit a dressed-up finish.
Wikipedia describes the early cravat as a forerunner of the modern necktie, and notes that "cravat" is the British name for what American English calls an ascot tie.

paras: Wearers fold or tie the cloth at the neck and tuck it into an open collar, typically with a blazer or smart-casual outfit. Silk and similar fabrics are common.
There are no particular health risks; a tight knot can be uncomfortable, and the look suits some dress codes more than others.

forums.title: Would You Endorse A Worthless Piece Of Equipment

chain: Adds colour and texture near the face
angle.text: The neckcloth fills the open collar and draws the eye upward to the face. It is a clothing accessory with no measured effect studies.

lead: An ascot (US) or cravat (UK) is a neckcloth worn inside an open collar rather than over a closed one. Wikipedia describes the early cravat as a forerunner of the modern necktie and notes the regional naming difference [1].

People use it for style: the fabric adds colour and texture at the neckline and frames the lower face. The word also has other meanings, including a triangular bandage and the 17th-century Croatian cavalry from which the term is said to derive [1].

paras: The cravat is an early ancestor of the necktie; British usage calls the ascot-style cloth a cravat, while American usage says ascot tie [1].
